response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE expirespot >= '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND expirespot <= '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) SELECT AVG(avg_remain) AS avg_of_order_avgs, SUM(exec_count) AS total_executions FROM per_order;

assumptions.assumption: expirespot is compared as text, lexicographically and inclusively, against the two bounds, as the request specifies. The schema declares it text(6) while the documentation describes it as a timestamp; the text comparison is used as requested.

Per-order average ignores NULL remaincount values (AVG does this natively). The execution count includes every row for the order, including rows with NULL remaincount. An order whose remaincount values are all NULL gets a NULL average and is skipped by the outer AVG, and the outer SUM still counts its executions. Rows with NULL ordersmark form their own group.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude executions with NULL ordersmark, since they do not belong to any order.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE expirespot >= '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND expirespot <= '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' AND ordersmark IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ordersmark) SELECT AVG(avg_remain) AS avg_of_order_avgs, SUM(exec_count) AS total_executions FROM per_order;
